CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zumime tells what a file is from its bytes and from its name, with no system dependency: a WHATWG MIME sniffer over the first kilobytes of a file or raw vector, container and brand inspection (ZIP entry names, ISO base media brands, RIFF, EBML, Ogg, OLE2), a type hierarchy ending at application/octet-stream, and a generated extension table. One call answers from both signals and says whether they agree. It is a base-layer package: zu* consumers such as zuhttp, zupdf, zuxlsx, zurds and dastash call it to decide a Content-Type or to refuse a file before their parsers see it. Zero hard runtime dependencies; the family’s own sniffers (zukomp, zuutf, zucsv, zujson) are reached through Suggests. It does not parse multipart bodies, read filesystem attributes, extract descriptive metadata (dimensions, duration, EXIF) or hash content; those belong to other packages.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted on 2026-10-18 from RFC 0040 in pedrobtz/packages. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design doc decides. Every decision in the RFC’s section 13 is marked (C), written without a design conversation, so each stays open to the maintainer until a stage records it.

Current state

All stages of .agents/roadmap.md, 0 to 8, are closed (verified 2026-11-11), so the design’s v0.1.0 scope is implemented. Version 0.1.0 is submitted to CRAN; the CRAN-submission issue, #10, tracks it until acceptance. The README is README.Rmd; the one article is vignettes/checking-an-upload.Rmd, built by pkgdown only.

Deviation from workflow.md (Releasing to CRAN). The repository has no cran-release.yaml and no committed CRAN-SUBMISSION (checked 2026-11-11), so nothing tags the release or opens the .9000 bump on its own. After acceptance, pkg-post-cran tags the submitted commit with the bare version, 0.1.0 (no v), publishes the GitHub release, bumps to 0.1.0.9000, closes the version’s parent issue and moves the board card.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1, v0.1.0. The design names anydoc, zuhttp, zusocks, zuarchive, dastash, zudedup, zupdf, zuxlsx and zurds as consumers; none depends on it yet, and no C API or header is in v0.1.0, so the R API is the whole breaking surface.

Commands

air format . reads air.toml. Package-specific commands:

tools/run-benchmarks                           # design §10 timings, as Markdown
ZUMIME_BENCH_FILES=10000 tools/run-benchmarks  # the same, smaller tree

Record each run in .agents/benchmarks.md with its date and machine.

Rscript tools/generate-tables.R            # rewrite sysdata.rda, zumime_types.h
Rscript tools/generate-tables.R --check    # exit 1 if they differ from their sources
Rscript tools/generate-tables.R --fetch    # download sources again, record sha256
tools/fetch-fixtures                       # fixtures, tests/testthat/fixtures/
tools/dump-file-type-answers               # answers into helper-file-type.R
tools/fuzz/run-local 60                    # fuzz harness, ASan+UBSan, 60 s
Rscript tools/fuzz/make-seeds.R            # rewrite tools/fuzz/seeds/
Rscript -e 'devtools::build_readme()'      # README.Rmd -> README.md

The registry is generated: edit tools/types.yaml (parents, aliases, extensions, detected_by) and regenerate, never the outputs. The tests that need fixtures skip without them; oracles.yaml fetches and runs them in CI.

Architecture

See .agents/design.md §4; this section records what has landed.

  • Registry (layer 1). tools/generate-tables.R reads tools/sources/ (IANA CSVs, Apache mime.types, checksummed in tools/table-sources.yaml) and tools/types.yaml, and writes R/sysdata.rda (types_registry, types_ext_map, types_alias_map, types_table_version) and src/zumime_types.h (enum ZUMIME_T_<TYPE> in sorted order, names and parent ids, defined once in src/registry.c). R/registry.R holds the registry functions; canonical_type() is the one place a type string is normalised.
  • Sniffer core (layer 2). src/zumime_sniff.h declares it; zumime_table.c holds the signature rows (the standard’s tables in its order, then zumime’s EXTRA rows), zumime_sniff.c the algorithm, zumime_charset.c the charset chain and newline style. These files include no R header and must compile with -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic (test-standalone.R). src/zumime_r.c is the R glue and the only place a type id becomes a CHARSXP.
  • Readers (layer 3). zumime_refine.c runs after the standard’s answer in the "none" context and hands the bytes to one reader: zumime_zip.c, zumime_ole2.c, zumime_bmff.c, zumime_ebml.c, zumime_ogg.c, zumime_png.c, zumime_rdata.c (gzip through zumime_inflate.c), zumime_text.c (structured text). A reader’s answer is kept only when it descends from the current type; add a parent in tools/types.yaml rather than an exception.
  • Paths (layer 4). src/zumime_path.c is the loop: it opens each path (_wfopen on Windows, native fopen elsewhere), reads the head, the ZIP tail and offset rows, checks completeness, and fills parallel vectors with no R allocation while a file is open. R/type.R builds the frame and the name columns; R/check.R holds mime_check()’s shortcut (zumime_check() in C) and probe_count(); R/register.R the session registry, mirrored in C by zumime_reg[] in registry.c.
  • Streams. src/zumime_stream.c is the can-decide rule; zumime_stream_push() in zumime_r.c keeps the bytes in the external pointer’s protected raw vector and the state in its address. R/stream.R is the API.
  • Fuzzing. tools/fuzz/harness.c is the libFuzzer target over the core (no R), run by .github/workflows/fuzz.yaml; tools/fuzz/driver.c runs it without libFuzzer locally.
  • Native layer. src/init.c registers every .Call entry point, declared in src/zumime_r.h, which also has zumime_scalar_string(): never pass a fresh CHARSXP to Rf_ScalarString() unprotected. src/mime_record.c is the WHATWG MIME type record over decoded code points; src/guess.c extracts suffixes for mime_guess().
  • Conditions. zumime_abort(kind, message) in R/conditions.R raises zumime_<kind>_error; check_character() raises zumime_type_error.
  • Results. new_result() in R/result.R builds every result frame; R/sniff.R handles the supplied type (supplied_type()) and argument checks.

Invariants that are easy to break

The design fixes these (RFC 0040 D6, D7, D8); add each further one when a stage establishes it.

  • Zero hard runtime dependencies. A zu* consumer takes no Imports by using zumime. Family sniffers (zukomp for the inner type of a compressed stream, zuutf for statistical charset detection, zucsv, zujson, zutoml) are Suggests and their absence degrades the answer to a coarser level, never to an error.
  • The answer is the same on every machine. zumime never reads the system’s mime.types or the Windows registry. A detector or table that consults the host makes results differ between CI legs and users.
  • Nothing is taken from the GPL mime package. The extension table is generated from IANA’s media types registry and Apache httpd’s mime.types (Apache-2.0), with the Apache Software Foundation in Authors@R as copyright holder, the lesson CRAN taught zukomp, zucrypt and zuxml in October 2026. Copying from mime is a licence violation.
  • Native symbols use the zumime_ prefix (ZUMIME_ for macros and the type enum).

Testing

  • Conformance suites. The design’s section 7 names three: web-platform-tests’ mimesniff/ fixtures for parsing, Go’s net/http sniff cases for the WHATWG table, and file-type’s fixtures for containers. All three are wired in: WPT and file-type fixtures through tools/fetch-fixtures, Go’s cases in helper-go-sniff.R. Their notices are in tests/testthat/COPYRIGHTS.
  • Helpers. helper-abi.R (symbol audit), helper-tables.R (source_root()), helper-fixtures.R (fixture_dir(), wpt_mime_entries()), helper-bytes.R (byte builders), helper-go-sniff.R (Go’s sniff cases), helper-containers.R (ZIP, OLE2, ftyp, Ogg and EBML builders), helper-file-type.R (file-type’s answers and the unclaimed fixtures), helper-skip.R.
  • Runtime. With NOT_CRAN=false the whole suite, load included, took 41 s on an Apple-silicon Mac (2026-10-26). The translated-path memory test (about 20 s) and the interrupt test skip on CRAN; the CI legs still run them.

Continuous integration

This package calls:

  • .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml → r-cmd-check.yml@v1, with Windows R-devel added to the default runners and CRAN’s NOSUGGESTS and NOLD flavors (nosuggests, nold, full profile only).
  • .github/workflows/native-checks.yaml → sanitizers.yml (with ASan), valgrind.yml, lto.yml, gctorture.yml, rchk.yml, analyzers.yml and cran-special.yml, all @v1 and all given the same profile.
  • .github/workflows/coverage.yaml → coverage.yml, pinned to the v1.23.0 commit, with contents: write. The badge goes to gh-pages, because the main ruleset requires pull requests and rejects a bot commit.
  • .github/workflows/fuzz.yaml → fuzz.yml@v1 over tools/fuzz/harness.c, built without R (-DZUMIME_STANDALONE, the R glue excluded). Two minutes on a pull request, 30 minutes nightly, an hour on dispatch or with the fuzz-hour label; the corpus is cached, so the runs add up to one campaign.

Its own workflows:

  • .github/workflows/oracles.yaml runs the design §7 oracles and tools/generate-tables.R --check, which R CMD check cannot run because the fixtures and tools/ are not in the tarball, plus the suite in shuffled order. ZUMIME_REQUIRE_ORACLES=true makes a missing fixture fail rather than skip.
  • .github/workflows/tables-upstream.yaml checks weekly whether IANA’s registry or Apache’s mime.types changed against tools/table-sources.yaml, and opens or updates an issue asking for a regeneration pull request. r-actions’ vendor-upstream.yml watches GitHub releases, which these files lack, and this repository does not let workflows open pull requests.
  • .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml is a bespoke r-lib/actions workflow, because r-actions has no pkgdown workflow to call. It deploys with force: false so it cannot overwrite a badge commit.

Deviation from ci.md. The R CMD check and native-check callers pass quick only on a pull request without full-ci, and full otherwise, rather than profile: auto. A push to main therefore runs the full set. Don’t wait on that run, and cancel older full runs it supersedes.

Vendored native code

src/zumime_inflate.c is adapted from Mark Adler’s puff.c version 2.3 (zlib’s contrib/puff, zlib-style licence, Copyright 2002-2013 Mark Adler). It is not under src/vendor/: it lives with the first-party sources, keeps puff’s notice in full, and is declared in inst/COPYRIGHTS. Local changes, recorded in the file’s header: errors set a flag instead of longjmp(); input is refilled through a reader; output goes to a 32 KiB window and only its first bytes are kept; decoding can stop when that capture is full; the gzip member and trailer check is new.
